new.title: Wander Büyükada's wooden Belle Époque mansions
new.desc: Büyükada, the largest of the Princes' Islands, is lined with 19th-century timber villas built by Greek, Armenian, Jewish and Levantine families. Streets such as Yılmaz Türk Caddesi and Nizam Caddesi hold the best-preserved examples, many with fretwork balconies and large gardens.
new.tip: Walk or cycle inland from the pier; most villas are private, so enjoy them from the road. Weekdays are far quieter than summer weekends.
new.q: Yılmaz Türk Caddesi, Nizam, Büyükada, Adalar, İstanbul

new.title: Climb to Aya Yorgi monastery on Yücetepe
new.desc: The Greek Orthodox church and monastery of Aya Yorgi (St George) stands on Yücetepe, the island's highest hill, with the present church dating to 1751. Pilgrims traditionally climb the last stretch on foot and tie rags to the trees.
new.tip: Entry is free; it is usually open in daytime except during Sunday worship. The hill is steep, so take an electric carriage part-way or hike up from Birlik Meydanı.
new.q: Aya Yorgi Kilisesi ve Manastırı, Yücetepe, Büyükada, Adalar, İstanbul

new.title: See the giant wooden Prinkipo Greek Orphanage
new.desc: The Prinkipo Greek Orphanage, built in 1898 as a hotel by architect Alexandre Vallaury and later an orphanage, is among the largest wooden buildings in Europe. It has stood empty and decaying for years and is visible from the surrounding hilltop paths.
new.tip: The building itself is closed to visitors, so view it from the road and forest paths above. Combine it with a bike ride on the island's southern loop.
new.q: Prinkipo Rum Yetimhanesi, Büyükada, Adalar, İstanbul

new.title: Cycle the Büyükada island loop
new.desc: Büyükada has no cars, so renting a bicycle near the pier is the classic way to circle the island. The roughly 14 km ride passes pine forests, mansions, rocky coves and viewpoints over the Marmara Sea.
new.tip: Rent a bike beside the ferry pier; weekday mornings are calmest. Hills are steep in the middle, so ride the coastal ring and walk the climbs.

new.title: Swim at Yörük Ali beach on Büyükada
new.desc: Yörük Ali is one of the island's best-known swimming spots, a pebbly shore with beach clubs on the southern side. The water is clean enough for swimming in summer, with views toward the other Princes' Islands.
new.tip: Beach clubs charge entry. Come early, since the island fills with day-trippers on summer weekends.
new.q: Yörük Ali Plajı, Büyükada, Adalar, İstanbul

new.title: Have a long breakfast at Sinek 5 on Büyükada
new.desc: Sinek 5 is a café-restaurant in a house on Büyükada known for Turkish breakfast spreads and seasonal home-style lunch dishes. Guides rate it above the pier fish restaurants.
new.tip: Reserve on summer weekends. Try the island breakfast plate and the daily specials.
new.q: Sinek 5, Yılmaz Türk Caddesi, Büyükada, Adalar, İstanbul

new.title: Eat fresh fish at Kalpazankaya on Burgazada
new.desc: Kalpazankaya is a waterfront fish restaurant on Burgazada, named after the nearby rock where counterfeiters were said to hide. It serves meze and the day's catch and is a long-time favourite of island hoppers.
new.tip: Check the day's fish and ask prices first. Lunch at the water's edge after the Sait Faik house works well.

new.title: Lunch on the seafront at Heyamola, Heybeliada
new.desc: Heyamola Ada Lokantası is a casual restaurant on Heybeliada's Yalı Caddesi near the pier. It serves home-style Turkish dishes and fish on the calmer, greener of the two big islands.
new.tip: Order meze and the fish of the day. It is an easy stop between the ferry and the Ümit Tepe walk.
new.q: Heyamola Ada Lokantası, Yalı Caddesi, Heybeliada, Adalar, İstanbul

new.title: Taste sweets at Büyükada Şekercisi
new.desc: Büyükada Şekercisi is a candy shop and patisserie near the pier, known for Turkish delight, ice cream and the island's traditional sweets. Its colourful interior is a favourite photo stop.
new.tip: Buy boxed lokum as souvenirs. It is busy right after ferries arrive, so go mid-afternoon.

new.title: Walk up Ümit Tepe to the Halki Seminary gates
new.desc: The Halki (Heybeliada) Theological School of the Holy Trinity, founded in 1844 on Ümit Tepe, trained Orthodox clergy until it closed in 1971. Restoration was reported in progress in 2026 with reopening still under negotiation. The pine path up the hill has sea views.
new.tip: The seminary is not open to visitors, so go for the hilltop walk and the view. Check current news before going.
new.q: Heybeliada Ruhban Okulu, Ümit Tepe, Heybeliada, Adalar, İstanbul

new.title: Swim in the pine-fringed Çam Limanı on Heybeliada
new.desc: Çam Limanı (Pine Harbour) is a sheltered bay on Heybeliada's southern shore, backed by pine woods and used by yachts and swimmers. It is quieter than the busy beaches on Büyükada.
new.tip: Reach it by a short walk or bike ride from the pier. Bring water and snacks as facilities are limited.

new.title: Visit writer Sait Faik's house on Burgazada
new.desc: The Sait Faik Abasıyanık Museum is the island home of the short-story writer (1906-1954), opened as a museum in 1959 under his will and now run by the Darüşşafaka Society. It holds his furniture, manuscripts and personal items, and the island features in many of his stories.
new.tip: Entry is free; check which days it is open. Take the ferry to Burgazada and walk uphill from the pier.
new.q: Sait Faik Abasıyanık Müzesi, Çınar Sokak 15, Burgazada, Adalar, İstanbul

new.title: See Kınalıada's red cliffs and Armenian church
new.desc: Kınalıada, the nearest and smallest of the Princes' Islands, is named for the reddish iron-rich soil of its slopes. It had a large Armenian community, and its Surp Krikor Lusavoriç church is among its landmarks.
new.tip: Ferries stop here first, so it works as a short stop. Walk up from the pier to the church and stroll the shore.

new.title: Ride the ferry to the Princes' Islands
new.desc: Marmara ferries run from Kabataş and Bostancı to Kınalıada, Burgazada, Heybeliada and Büyükada, about 90 minutes on the slow boat. Sitting outside with a simit and tea is the traditional way to travel.
new.tip: Pay with an Istanbulkart. Go on a weekday in spring or autumn and sit on the upper deck for island views.

new.title: Hike the Bentler Nature Park in Belgrad Forest
new.desc: Belgrad Forest is the oak and beech woodland north of Istanbul, protected since Ottoman times because it fed the city's water system. Bentler Nature Park, named for the old dams, has marked trails and picnic grounds around the Topuzlu, Valide and New Dams.
new.tip: Entry to the park is cheap and weekdays are quiet. Waymarked loops from Valide Dam run about 20 km, with shorter easy loops.
new.q: Bentler Tabiat Parkı, Belgrad Ormanı, Sarıyer, İstanbul

new.title: See Mağlova Aqueduct built by Mimar Sinan
new.desc: The Mağlova Aqueduct near Kemerburgaz was designed by Mimar Sinan for Süleyman the Magnificent and finished in 1563. Two tiers of arches span a valley and carried water toward Istanbul as part of the Kırkçeşme system.
new.tip: It sits in woodland near Kemerburgaz and is free to see. Combine it with nearby Uzunkemer and the Belgrad Forest trails.

new.title: Walk beneath the Uzunkemer aqueduct
new.desc: Uzunkemer (Long Arch) is an Ottoman aqueduct of two tiers near Kemerburgaz, attributed to Mimar Sinan in the 1560s. It forms part of the Kırkçeşme water system and still stands among the trees.
new.tip: Free and open outdoors. Combine it with Mağlova and the Kemerburgaz forest paths.

new.title: Stroll along the 1796 Valide Dam in Belgrad Forest
new.desc: Valide Dam (Valide Bendi) was built in 1796 under Selim III in honour of his mother and is one of the historic reservoirs that gave Bentler its name. The stone dam holds a still lake with trails around it.
new.tip: Combine with a loop hike through Bentler. Go in autumn for leaf colour.
new.q: Valide Bendi, Belgrad Ormanı, Sarıyer, İstanbul

new.title: Swim at Kilyos on the Black Sea
new.desc: Kilyos is a Black Sea village in Sarıyer, long a summer escape for Istanbulites, with long sandy beaches and beach clubs. The Black Sea here has waves and cooler water than the Marmara.
new.tip: Beach clubs charge entry; the municipal beach is cheaper. Watch the flags, as currents can be strong.

new.title: Climb to Kilyos's Genoese castle ruins
new.desc: The ruined castle above Kilyos dates to the Genoese presence on the Black Sea coast in the 14th century and was reused by the Ottomans. Its walls overlook the sea and village.
new.tip: Free to wander; wear sturdy shoes as the ground is uneven. Walk it before or after a beach day.

new.title: Visit Rumeli Feneri fishing village and lighthouse
new.desc: Rumeli Feneri is a fishing village at the Black Sea mouth of the Bosphorus, with a lighthouse built in 1856 and ruins of a Genoese fort above the harbour. Its fish restaurants are a weekend favourite.
new.tip: Reach it by bus from Sarıyer or by car. The harbour at sunset is the main draw.

new.title: Climb Şile Lighthouse above the Black Sea
new.desc: Şile Lighthouse, built in 1859 by a French company for the Ottoman state, stands on a cliff above the town and can be climbed. A small maritime exhibit sits in the grounds.
new.tip: Check hours before going; guides list roughly 10:00 to 16:00 and closed Mondays. Climb to the top for the coast view.

new.title: See Şile Castle on its offshore rock
new.desc: Şile Castle is a ruined fortification on a small islet just offshore from Şile town, linked to Genoese and Ottoman defence of the coast. It is best seen from the shore near the harbour.
new.tip: It is mainly a photo stop from the beach; access to the rock is limited. Pair it with the lighthouse visit.

new.title: Shop for hand-embroidered Şile bezi
new.desc: Şile bezi is the light cotton cloth woven and hand-embroidered in Şile for generations, used for blouses, tablecloths and scarves. Shops line the town centre.
new.tip: Compare shops, as quality varies a lot. Ask for genuine hand embroidery and check the stitching.
new.q: Şile Bezi Çarşısı, Şile Merkez, Şile, İstanbul

new.title: Swim at Şile's Ayazma and Kumbaba beaches
new.desc: Şile has long sandy Black Sea beaches beside the town, including Ayazma and Kumbaba, the nearest proper beach day from Istanbul. Waves are lively and facilities range from basic to moderate.
new.tip: Weekdays are calmer. Be careful with currents on windy days.

new.title: Take a boat trip on the Göksu river in Ağva
new.desc: Ağva sits where the Göksu and Yeşilçay rivers meet the Black Sea, and small tourist boats run upriver past reed beds and wooded banks. Kayaks and canoes are also rented by the river.
new.tip: Boats run mostly in season. Combine it with lunch at a riverside restaurant.
new.q: Ağva Göksu Nehri, Ağva, Şile, İstanbul

new.title: Eat grilled sea bass at Şenol, Ağva
new.desc: Şenol is a restaurant near Ağva's fishing harbour where the Yeşilçay meets the sea. Local fish such as grilled sea bass, bluefish and, in season, anchovies feature on the menu.
new.tip: Order the day's fish and meze. Weekends get crowded, so go early.

new.title: Have clay-oven trout by the river at Elvora, Ağva
new.desc: Elvora Restaurant sits on the river along Yakuplu Caddesi in Ağva, serving fish and grills with tables beside the Göksu. Trout baked in a clay oven is a local speciality.
new.tip: Try the tile-kiln trout. Riverside tables fill on weekends.
new.q: Elvora Restaurant, Yakuplu Caddesi, Ağva, Şile, İstanbul

new.title: Swim at Ağva's Black Sea beach
new.desc: Ağva's long beach lies where the Yeşilçay river mouth meets the Black Sea, with sand and dunes backed by reeds. It is quieter than Şile and Kilyos on weekdays.
new.tip: Currents near the river mouth can be strong. Bring your own shade or rent a sunbed.

new.title: Walk the forest paths of Polonezköy Nature Park
new.desc: Polonezköy was founded in 1842 by Polish exiles, and the village is set within the beech woods of a nature park. Marked trails lead through the forest to viewpoints and a stream.
new.tip: Entry to the park is cheap and weekdays are quiet. Dress for mud in wet weather.
new.q: Polonezköy Tabiat Parkı, Polonezköy, Beykoz, İstanbul

new.title: Taste Polish and Turkish dishes at Leonardo, Polonezköy
new.desc: Leonardo is one of Polonezköy's best-known restaurants, serving Polish, Turkish and French dishes in a village garden setting. The Polish settlers left a tradition of filled buns and hearty stews.
new.tip: Book at weekends. Try the Polish-style meat dishes and apple cake.

new.title: Order bigos at Bistro Na Trakcie, Polonezköy
new.desc: Bistro Na Trakcie serves Polish specialities such as bigos (hunter's stew) and potato pancakes in the village. It is a small bistro in the spirit of the community's Polish roots.
new.tip: Come for weekend lunch. Check opening days first as hours vary.
new.q: Bistro Na Trakcie, Polonezköy, Beykoz, İstanbul

new.title: Visit the Polish church and museum in Polonezköy
new.desc: The Church of the Holy Mary in Polonezköy was built for the Polish Catholic community, and the Zofia Ryży museum opposite shows photographs and documents on Adampol's history. A small Polish graveyard lies nearby.
new.tip: The museum is mainly open on Sundays. The church can be seen from outside on other days.

new.title: Swim at Riva beach on the Black Sea
new.desc: Riva is a Black Sea resort at the mouth of the Riva stream in Beykoz, with a long sandy beach and pine hills. The shore has a wild feel and a few beach clubs.
new.tip: Reach it by bus from Beykoz. Watch for strong swell.

new.title: Cross Mimar Sinan's 16th-century bridge at Büyükçekmece
new.desc: The Mimar Sinan Bridge at Büyükçekmece was built for Süleyman the Magnificent and finished in 1567. The 636 m stone bridge has 28 arches and spans the lagoon where Lake Büyükçekmece meets the sea.
new.tip: Free to walk across. Combine with a lakeside walk and the lagoon-side cafés.

new.title: Tour Atatürk's Marine Mansion in Florya
new.desc: The Atatürk Marine Mansion (Florya Deniz Köşkü) is a modernist summer residence built on piles over the Marmara Sea in 1935 for Atatürk. It is now a small museum with his furniture and belongings.
new.tip: Check opening days; it is usually closed Mondays. The adjoining Florya Atatürk Forest park is good for a walk.
new.q: Atatürk Deniz Köşkü, Florya, Bakırköy, İstanbul

new.title: See İzmit's 1901 Clock Tower
new.desc: The İzmit Clock Tower is a neoclassical clock tower built in 1901-1902 for Sultan Abdülhamid II's jubilee. It stands in the city centre and is one of İzmit's best-known landmarks.
new.tip: Free to see. Combine with a pişmaniye shop visit and the nearby harbour walk.
new.q: İzmit Saat Kulesi, Kemalpaşa, İzmit, Kocaeli

new.title: Tour the SEKA Paper Museum in İzmit
new.desc: The SEKA Paper Museum, opened in 2016 in a former paper mill, tells the story of paper-making in Turkey with machinery and exhibits from one of the country's oldest industrial sites. It sits in the Kozluk district of İzmit.
new.tip: Check hours before going. Allow an hour for the tour.
new.q: SEKA Kağıt Müzesi, Mehmet Ali Kağıtçı Sokak 77, Kozluk, İzmit, Kocaeli

new.title: Buy fresh pişmaniye at İpek Pişmaniye, İzmit
new.desc: Pişmaniye is a floss-like sweet made from flour, sugar and butter, and İzmit holds the geographical indication for it. İpek Pişmaniye, in business since 1954, is one of the long-standing makers.
new.tip: Ask to watch the sweet being pulled if the shop allows. Buy small boxes as gifts.

new.title: Pay respects at Hannibal's tomb in Gebze
new.desc: The Hannibal Monument in Gebze marks the place traditionally linked to the burial of Carthage's general Hannibal, who died in Libyssa around 183 BC. A small memorial garden holds the tomb.
new.tip: Entry is free. Combine it with the Çoban Mustafa Paşa complex in Gebze.

new.title: Visit the Çoban Mustafa Paşa Complex in Gebze
new.desc: The Çoban Mustafa Paşa Külliyesi was built by Çoban Mustafa Pasha in 1523-1524 and includes a mosque, madrasa, bath, soup kitchen and the pasha's tomb. It is one of the early classical Ottoman complexes near Istanbul.
new.tip: Free to visit. Mind prayer times when inside the mosque.
new.q: Çoban Mustafa Paşa Külliyesi, Gebze, Kocaeli

new.title: Walk the Eskihisar waterfront and Osman Hamdi Bey's house
new.desc: Eskihisar is a small village on the Gulf of İzmit with a castle ruin and the house of the painter and museum founder Osman Hamdi Bey (1842-1910). The house museum is listed as closed for restoration, so the village walk is the main draw.
new.tip: Check whether the house has reopened before travelling. The harbour tea gardens are open.
new.q: Osman Hamdi Bey Evi ve Müzesi, Eskihisar, Gebze, Kocaeli

new.title: Ride up Kartepe to hike or ski
new.desc: Kartepe is the mountain above İzmit with a ski resort, a cable car and hiking trails with views over Sapanca and the Gulf of İzmit. It is Istanbul's nearest ski area.
new.tip: Snow usually falls from December to March. Take warm layers, as it is much colder than the coast.

new.title: Walk to the waterfalls of Maşukiye
new.desc: Maşukiye is a forest village below Kartepe with a stream valley, small waterfalls and a nature walk. Riverside restaurants and tea gardens line the stream.
new.tip: Free to walk. Weekdays are calmer than weekends.

new.title: Eat clay-pot trout at Akasya Alabalık, Maşukiye
new.desc: Maşukiye's stream-side restaurants are known for trout, often grilled or baked in a clay pot. Akasya Alabalık is one of the named trout houses on Alabalık Sokak.
new.tip: Order the trout in a clay pot. Check opening hours first, especially in winter.
new.q: Akasya Alabalık, Alabalık Sokak 45/A, Maşukiye, Kartepe, Kocaeli

new.title: Swim at Kerpe on the Kandıra coast
new.desc: Kerpe is a quiet Black Sea beach village on the Kandıra coast, with sandy beaches, rocky headlands and fishing boats. It is far less developed than the Istanbul beaches.
new.tip: A car is needed. Check weather and swell before going.

new.title: Taste Kandıra's traditional yoghurt
new.desc: Kandıra is known in Kocaeli for thick, creamy yoghurt made from local milk. Shops in the town centre sell it by the portion, often with honey.
new.tip: Eat it at breakfast. Take a small jar home if you have a cool bag.
new.q: Kandıra Yoğurdu, Kandıra Merkez, Kandıra, Kocaeli

new.title: Explore the stalactites of Dupnisa Cave
new.desc: Dupnisa Cave in the Strandzha forest near Demirköy is Thrace's only show cave, with several levels, stalactites and an underground stream. It is closed in winter because bats hibernate there.
new.tip: It is likely closed from mid-November to mid-May; confirm with the Kırklareli tourism office. The road to the cave is rural.

new.title: Paddle or walk the İğneada Longoz forests
new.desc: İğneada Floodplain Forests National Park, established in 2007, protects flooded oak and ash forests, Lake Mert, Lake Saka and dunes on the Black Sea. It is a rare wetland forest in Turkey.
new.tip: Guided boat and canoe tours are the best way in. Spring and autumn are good for birds.
new.q: İğneada Longoz Ormanları Milli Parkı, İğneada, Demirköy, Kırklareli

new.title: Swim at İğneada's unspoilt Black Sea beaches
new.desc: İğneada's long sandy beaches are among the least developed on Turkey's Black Sea shore, backed by forest and lakes.
new.tip: Facilities are basic. Camping is popular in summer.

new.title: Eat fish and olive-oil dishes at Çatkapı, İğneada
new.desc: Çatkapı is a restaurant in İğneada listed among the town's seafood restaurants and noted for olive oil dishes as well as fish. It serves Black Sea catch near the harbour.
new.tip: Order the grilled fish. Check opening days in the off-season.

new.title: Visit the rock-cut Aya Nikola monastery in Kıyıköy
new.desc: Aya Nikola is a 6th-century rock-cut monastery on the slope above Kıyıköy, with a church on the ground floor and monks' cells above. It was restored in 1856 and used until 1922.
new.tip: Allow a 15 to 30 minute walk from the village. A local volunteer guide often shows visitors around for a tip.
new.q: Aya Nikola Manastırı, Kıyıköy, Vize, Kırklareli

new.title: See the Hızırbey Complex in Kırklareli
new.desc: The Hızırbey Complex in Kırklareli town was built in 1383 and includes a mosque, madrasa and bath, a rare surviving 14th-century Ottoman group in Thrace.
new.tip: Free to enter outside prayer times. Combine with the town museum and centre.

new.title: Taste Thracian wines at Chamlija winery
new.desc: Chamlija is a Thracian winery near Kırklareli known for estate wines and artist-designed bottle labels. It farms about 85 hectares of vines across several plots.
new.tip: Book a tasting in advance. Combine with Arcadia and other wineries on the route.

new.title: Visit Arcadia Vineyards near Kırklareli
new.desc: Arcadia Vineyards was founded in 2007 by Özcan and Zeynep Arca and makes low-intervention wines from sustainable vineyards in the Kırklareli hills. A boutique vineyard hotel sits beside it.
new.tip: Reserve tastings in advance, as opening varies by season.
